answer: Neighborhood Basalt Routing. Each agent's messages must traverse distinct, locally-recorded neighbor paths; a quill signer attests only to direct edges, never to global membership. New identities must first attach to existing topology as a fresh island node, paying latency and bandwidth to route through established neighbors before earning relay priority. Sybils therefore cannot shortcut in: each fake identity costs a full independent path of organic traffic and sustained uptime to avoid pruning.
